newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello sees budget forecasts being met.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello sees budget forecasts being met.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday he had every reason to believe the government's 1997/98 budget forecasts would be met.

Costello was asked about the timing of a possible upgrade in Australia's sovereign credit rating, following an announcement on Wednesday by Moody's Investor Services that Australia's credit rating outlook was improving.

"I think that you would expect them (Moody's) over the next six months to watch developments, and what they will particularly be watching, I believe, is whether we meet our budget forecasts," Costello said.
"Now there's every reason to believe that we will, but I think they'll sit back and they'll keep their eye on that."
Costello said Moody's did not give a particular timing when asked by a reporter if an upgrade would occur within six months.
"They don't give you any particular timing, but that would be the timeframe that I would expect them to look at things."
The government's budget for the year to June 30, 1998 forecast an underlying 1997/98 budget deficit of A$3.853 billion, down from a forecast deficit of A$6.856 billion in 1996/97.
